He played college basketball for the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]]. ==Early years== Jerome attended [[Iona Preparatory School]] in [[New Rochelle, New York]] and was a four-year varsity player. After his junior season at Iona Prep, he was named first-team All-Conference, All-Metropolitan, and All-State.{{cite web |title=Virginia Cavaliers Bio school = virginia | espn schoolid = 258 | 247 overall = 44 | rivals overall = 53 | scout overall = 51 | espn overall = 43 | accessdate = February 9, 2019 | bball = yes }} ==College career== During his freshman year at Virginia, Jerome was the backup point guard to [[London Perrantes]]. Coming off the bench, he averaged 4.3 points, 1.6 rebounds, and 1.5 assists. Jerome took over as the Cavaliers' starting point guard his sophomore year. On December 30, 2017, he put up a career-high 31 points against [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]]. His play during the season earned him a spot on the All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] Third Team. Prior to the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018-2019 season]], Jerome to the [[2018–19 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season#Preseason All-ACC Teams|pre-season all-ACC Second Team]].{{cite web |title=DUKE TOPS ACC BASKETBALL PRESEASON MEDIA POLL |url=https://theacc.com/news/2018/10/25/mens-basketball-duke-tops-acc-basketball-preseason-media-poll.aspx |website=theACC.com |accessdate=February 9, 2019 |date=October 25, 2018}} On February 4, 2019, Jerome was named as one of the ten finalists for the [[Bob Cousy Award]], recognizing the nation's top college point guard. He is also listed in most mock drafts as an early second-round pick in the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last1=Darney |first1=Caroline |title=Ty Jerome named a finalist for the Bob Cousy Award |url=https://www.streakingthelawn.com/2019/2/5/18210820/ty-jerome-finalist-bob-cousy-award-back-injury-update |website=streakingthelawn.com |publisher=Vox Media, Inc |accessdate=February 9, 2019 |date=February 5, 2019}} Jerome averaged 13.6 points per game and 5.5 assists per game, helping lead Virginia to another #1 seed in the [[2019_NCAA_Division_I_Men%27s_Basketball_Tournament|2019 NCAA Tournament]]. Virginia would win the [[2019 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|2019 Championship game]] 85-77 behind Jerome's 16 points, 8 assists, and 6 rebounds. At the conclusion of the season, Jerome announced his intention to forgo his final season of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2019 NBA Draft]] while hiring an agent.{{Cite news|url=https://www.richmond.com/sports/college/schools/university-virginia/uva-basketball-star-ty-jerome-will-leave-school-early-for/article_67c22cd7-e669-57a8-89fe-eb0fd4728918.html|title=UVA basketball star Ty Jerome will leave school early for the NBA Draft|work=[[Richmond Times-Dispatch]]|author=Mike Barber|date=April 15, 2019}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2016–17 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] | 34 || 5 || 13.9 || '''.473''' || .397 || .778 || 1.6 || 1.5 || .4 || '''.1''' || 4.3 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2017–18 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] | 34 || 34 || 30.8 || .421 || .379 || '''.905''' || 3.1 || 3.9 || '''1.6''' || .0 || 10.6 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2018–19 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]] | '''37''' || '''37''' || '''33.9''' || .435 || '''.399''' || .736 || '''4.2''' || '''5.5''' || 1.5 || .0 || '''13.6''' |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 105 || 76 || 26.4 || .435 || .392 || .788 || 3.0 || 3.7 || 1.2 || .0 || 9.6 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Jerome's parents are Mark Jerome and Melanie Walker.
